assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Single table 'discountPercentByPassengerTypeAndTrips' mixes Passenger type and Prior trips columns; no rolling window table present

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note.

The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Multiple tiers shown (0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%) with boundary testing: 3→0%, 4→5%, 8→5%, 9→10%, 39→40%; max 40% represented

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table exists; no rows testing boundary at 30 vs 31 days

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: Tier table uses single ticket count values (0, 3, 4, 8, 9, 19, 39, 100) not value sets like {5,6,7,8,9} per tier

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: 'Prior trips in last 30 days' column: 0, 3, 4, 8, 9, 19, 39, 100 — individual values, not value sets

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Second table passes discount % as parameter without re-enumerating tier mappings from first table

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Discount percentage by passenger type and recent trips") and @DisplayName("Ticket price with discount applied")

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
assertions.evidence: First method has @Description explaining 'prior trips' concept, ladder structure, and flags open question about current purchase inclusion

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses """ text block with multi-line content, not string concatenation

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: No Zone column in table; 'Zone has no effect' mentioned only in @Description text, not shown in table structure

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row of the eligibility table.
assertions.evidence: Multiple rows show '| {ADULT, SENIOR} |' demonstrating identical discount rules for both types
Table shows only tiers: 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%; missing tiers 15%, 25%, 30%, 35%

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows.
assertions.evidence: 0% tier: rows 'No prior trips (0)' and 'Below first tier (3)'; 5% tier: 'At first tier (4)' and 'Within first tier (8)' — split for boundary testing

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or an integer 'Days ago' column).
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table present in response; 'Prior trips in last 30 days' uses absolute count, not relative time

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: First table mixes 'Passenger type' and 'Prior trips' columns (discount ladder + eligibility); rolling window table absent

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: First table: 9 rows with focused boundary testing; second table: 4 rows testing price arithmetic; appropriate minimality given concerns
